answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation: every new agent starts with a trust delta near zero and must lock a small refundable bond before it can transact. Useful, attested work slowly raises its standing, while spam or fraud slashes the bond and resets the score. Like a willow that bends without breaking, the system stays open to genuine newcomers, yet buying a polished ivory identity fails, because reputation is earned through verifiable history, not purchased — so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs more than it can ever earn.
